messages:
alex.prod: Heads-up — customer (tenant acme-inc) reports large aggregate latency on streaming SSE paths after the 03/15 runtime deploy. p50 looks fine but p95/p99 jumped. They repro by multiplexing ~20 logical streams over one connection; non-streaming requests show normal total times. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

sam.infra: I saw a brief reg on canary yesterday related to microbatching/flush-window changes. Could be coalescing delay + client-side buffering when many streams share conn. Do you have a simple repro snippet?

alex.prod: Yep, repro steps from customer attached (trimmed):
```bash
# open one SSE conn, then start 20 parallel chat streams over it
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?mux=1
```
Client trace shows first-event latency per stream ~300-800ms (p99), while non-stream single requests p99 ~60ms. headers: `Connection: keep-alive`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `X-Client-Mux: 20`.

maria.sre: Adding logs — deploybot shows the microbatching feature flag flip at 2026-03-15T02:12Z on canary then prod. Metrics: `stream_flush_delay_ms` median from ~5ms -> ~28ms after flip; p99 increased similarly. That aligns with coalescing.

jordan.support: Customer is impacted in prod tenant — they asked for mitigation asap. They tried lowering client concurrency and saw immediate improvement (p95 -> ~140ms).

sam.infra: Quick triage: two options — 1) force immediate flush on our proxy path for SSE when `X-Client-Mux` present or multiplexing header detected, 2) roll back microbatching config for affected capacity pools. Rollback is fastest to restore baseline.

maria.sre: Agreed. I'll open rollback RFC and trigger canary rollback to the dedicated pool for the tenant. Also adding temporary alert for `stream_first_event.p99 > 200ms` so we catch regressions if other tenants hit it. :alarm_clock:

alex.prod: For support band-aid, tell customer to reduce mux per conn to <=8 or set SDK config `flush_threshold_ms=5`. They reported that helped in their test.

jordan.support: I'll pass the workaround and ETA. Can you post the rollback timeline here once started?

maria.sre: Rollback to previous microbatching=off started at 1768505600 (canary), no consumer-visible error; prod rollback window scheduled 1768506500-1768507000. Monitoring in progress. :white_check_mark:

sam.infra: After canary rollback we saw `stream_flush_delay_ms.p50` back to ~6ms and `stream_first_event.p99` down to ~80ms for the canary pool. Will follow with postmortem and suggested mitigations: better heuristics for multiplexed connections and an explicit header to disable coalescing for SSE.

alex.prod: Perfect — I'll keep customer updated and collect their SDK traces for the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :party_parrot:

deploybot: Deployment event: rollback microbatching flag -> OFF (user: maria.sre) at 1768506605.
